take_homes: Split agents only on access, dialect or stance. Otherwise one agent with a good prompt.
Give the synthesizer a framework like Rumelt's kernel, so it picks one diagnosis instead of averaging three views.
Handoffs between agents fail silently, and nothing in the module checks whether the final answer is true.

monday.move: Pick one recurring sales workflow and write the split-or-not test (access, dialect, stance) before building anything. Ask one sales person whether they want it.
monday.who: Me, plus one person from sales
monday.when: Monday morning, before touching Claude Code
monday.stop_condition: Nobody in sales asks for it, or nobody owns maintaining it.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for it, and I haven't decided who maintains it.

misconception.why: I still think a good agent mostly gives good output. But the two numbers going in and one coming out, and an audit that checks handoffs but not truth, made me think I should verify more than I do. The module never made me check anything myself, so it's only shaken.

one_line: Good for people who've never split an agent, and the access-dialect-stance test and the seams bit were worth it. The middle repeats itself, and nothing makes you check the final answer.
